problem: S3-SECU-02: RemoteURL.make (ADR draft D-6) rejects `rejected(.invalidURL)` for empty components, `.` (also `%2E`), `\`, `?` and `#`. Fix round 3 (orchestrator decision 3) made the Model quarantine `?` and `#` 'instead of failing every fetch in the transport (TR1-10)', but did not do the same for the other spellings. The decoder still accepts `media//a.png`, `media/./a.png`, `./a.png`, `media/%2E/a.png`, `media\a.png` and `media/`. Such an entry is applied and planned, then fails at once on every attempt. ARCHITECTURE §7.6 maps `rejected(violation)` to `failed(.nextRun)` and answers waiters `.serverUnavailable(retryAfter: nil)`. So the entry is retried every run and misreported as a server problem instead of being quarantined with a diagnostic. The prior art fetched `a//b.png` with appendingPathComponent, so a manifest that relies on it decodes but no longer behaves as before. This is not a traversal: no such path can leave the base. It is a robustness and consistency gap that the recorded decision did not cover.
fix: The decoder refuses (as the existing per-entry path violation, quarantined) every remote path the transport refuses: empty segment, '.' segment, backslash, trailing slash, and their percent-encoded forms (`%2E`), so no accepted entry fails on every fetch. One rule, in the model; the transport keeps its check as defence. Test each form.

detail.requirements: R-MAN-2 (per-entry violations quarantine the entry with a diagnostic), R-MAN-1 (manifests behave as before), TR1-10, ADR draft A-4.7 / orchestrator decision 3, ADR draft D-6

detail.evidence: .build-orchestrator/s3-probes/security/S3-SECU-02.swift and S3-SECU-02-03.log. Failing lines: '✘ Test "R-MAN-2: a remote path the transport refuses on every fetch is quarantined by the decoder" with 6 test cases failed after 0.001 seconds with 12 issues.' For the argument "media//a.png": 'Expectation failed: manifest.entries.map(\.identifier) == ["ok"] … media//a.png was accepted although no fetch of it can ever be made … → [ok, x]' and 'manifest.quarantinedCount → 0'. The transport side is already proven by the passing ForegroundBackendTests.invalidPaths ('R-NET-4: a remote path that could leave the base path is refused as an invalid URL', arguments "a//b", "a\\b", "a/%2E/b"; 151/151 transport tests passed, also under TSan). For "./a.png" and "media/", RemoteURL.make returns nil on the decoded "." and on the empty last component (RequestFactory.swift:74-80).
detail.repro: Copy S3-SECU-02.swift to Tests/ZTronAssetModelTests/Manifest/S3SecurityModelProbeTests.swift, then: swift test --scratch-path <scratch> --skip Benchmarks --filter S3SecurityModelProbeTests
detail.fix: Add one RemotePathViolation (for example `.emptyOrDotSegment` plus `.backslash`, or extend `.parentSegment`'s pass) so that the decoder quarantines exactly what RemoteURL.make refuses: an empty segment, a `.` segment (also `%2e`), and a `\`. Keep `%3F` allowed, as in A-4.7. Alternatively relax RemoteURL.make to the Model's rules and record the choice in an ADR. Either way, add a test that every path the decoder accepts yields a URL from RemoteURL.make.

confirmer.reason: I reproduced this at s3-base. The hunter's model probe failed with 12 issues: all 6 paths were accepted (entries [ok, x], quarantinedCount 0). My own probe (S3-SECU-02.swift in the transport tests) decodes each path with ManifestDecoder and then calls the real internal RemoteURL.make. For media//a.png, media/./a.png, ./a.png, media/%2E/a.png, media\a.png and media/, it reports 'decoder accepted=true, RemoteURL.make=nil'. The control path media/ok.png passes. I checked the code. HTTPRemoteSource.transfer:182 returns `.failed(.rejected(.invalidURL))` when RemoteURL.make returns nil. EngineFailures.swift:192-194 maps `.rejected` to `failed(.nextRun)` and gives waiters `.serverUnavailable(retryAfter: nil)`. The breaker outcome is neutral. Nothing in Sync or Storage checks remotePath beforehand. So the entry is planned, fails at once on every run, and is misreported as a server problem. Why it is not blocking: the SPEC's R-MAN-2 remotePath violation list (relative, ≤1,024 bytes, no `..`, scheme, authority or control character) does not include these spellings, so the decoder meets the MUST. Draft A-4.7 explicitly says '`.` … stay allowed' in the Model. Draft D-6 records that the transport rejects empty, `.` and `\` components. There is no crash, no data loss and no traversal; only the Model/transport mismatch for these spellings went unhandled. This is a confirmed consistency/robustness gap and NON-blocking. The owner is WP-A (Sources/ZTronAssetModel/**). The alternative fix would touch WP-D's RequestFactory.swift. Evidence: .build-orchestrator/s3-probes/confirm-security/S3-SECU-02.swift, S3-SECU-02-03-model-probe.swift, S3-SECU-02-03.log and S3-SECU-02-03-confirm.log.

problem: S3-SECU-03: TransferAttempt(token:) accepts leading zeros (`01-2`, `1-02`) and TransferID(rawValue:) accepts any `c-[a-z0-9-]*`, not only `c-<64 hex>`. So StagingFileName(parsing:) is not 'nil for anything that is not exactly one of our names' (its own doc). A foreign `c-<h>.01-2.part` parses as ours, and its rawValue is `c-<h>.1-2.part`, which is a different file. StagingCollection.garbage then applies age rules instead of 'foreign: always removed'. listStaging (AssetStore+Reads.swift:172) keys the inventory by the parsed name, so two directory entries collapse onto one key, and stagingURL(name) addresses the canonical file, not the listed one. BackgroundTaskTag(decoding:) inherits the same leniency. Only a file planted inside the app's container can reach this, and no data is lost: age-based GC removes it eventually. Robustness only.
fix: `StagingFileName(parsing:)` and `TransferAttempt(token:)` accept only canonical forms (no leading zeros), so a parsed name's `rawValue` names the same file. AUTHORISED: bodies of the contract files `Sources/ZTronAssetModel/Identity/TransferID.swift` and `Identity/StagingFileName.swift`, no signature change.

detail.requirements: R-SEC-2 (names under the root), R-CLN-3 (anything under staging/ that does not parse is foreign and collected), ADR-013

The run shows '✘ Test "R-SEC-2: staging names parse only in the canonical spelling the module writes" recorded an issue with 1 argument fileName → "c-aaaa…aaaa.1-02.part" … ↳ c-aaaa…aaaa.1-02.part parsed as c-aaaa…aaaa.1-2.part', and the same for ".01-2.part".
detail.fix: In StagingFileName(parsing:), require `parsed.rawValue == fileName`, or make TransferAttempt(token:) reject leading zeros. Make TransferID(rawValue:) require exactly 64 lowercase hex digits after `c-`/`l-` (ContentHash(hex:)). Commit the probe as the regression test.

confirmer.reason: I reproduced this at s3-base. In the hunter's probe, 'c-<64a>.01-2.part' and 'c-<64a>.1-02.part' both parse as 'c-<64a>.1-2.part'. The cause is that TransferAttempt(token:) (TransferID.swift:125-136) accepts leading zeros, which contradicts StagingFileName(parsing:)'s own doc ('nil for anything that is not exactly one of our names'). My probe (S3-SECU-03.swift) adds two results. StagingCollection.garbage keeps a fresh non-canonical name under the age rules instead of 'foreign names always'. And two different directory entries parse to the same key, so listStaging's inventory collapses them. One part of the claim is refuted: TransferID(rawValue:) accepting any `c-[a-z0-9-]*` matches its documented contract ('1…96 bytes of [0-9a-z-] with a known prefix'), and the probe's 'c-zz.1-2.part' case round-trips and passes. Impact: StagingCollection removes files by the listed item.name, so age-based GC still deletes the file. On the launch adoptStaged path, publish addresses the canonical name and discards on failure. The only way to reach this is a file planted inside the app's own container, not a path derived from manifest text, so the R-SEC-2 MUST (no escape from the root) and I-4 still hold. This is a robustness gap and NON-blocking. The owner is WP-A (Sources/ZTronAssetModel/Identity/**). Evidence: .build-orchestrator/s3-probes/confirm-security/S3-SECU-03.swift, S3-SECU-02-03-model-probe.swift and the two logs.
